title: Make game detect when player closes it

posts.author: kinglyvibe
posts.body: Hi! I’m working on a game and I really want a mechanic that allows the game to sense if the player has closed it during a run, so that every time the game opens something is different. Is there any way to do that?

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body: How would this be functionally different from randomizing on the title screen/loading the first map?

posts.author: kinglyvibe
posts.body:
AquaEcho said:
How would this be functionally different from randomizing on the title screen/loading the first map?
Click to expand...
The events have to go in a progressive order. For example, the first time you load the game, it will be winter. The second time you load it will be spring, the third time fall, etc. I want to be able to detect the number of times a player has reloaded so I can tell specific events to load in order.
I’m not sure if that answers this question, and I’m sorry if I’m being confusing! I’m quite new to doing anything complex, haha.

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
Should this really be linked to closing the game?
For example: If I start the game twice, and quit on the main title screen without playing, will it be winter or summer when I start it again?
And what if I play it, had summer, and start a new game file the next time? Will it be winter again or continue to be autumn?
Execute this on loading the savegame might be a better way to go.

posts.author: kirbwarrior
posts.body:
As the others have pointed out, this would be much easier to implement based on open instead of close with the assumption that the player closes their game when they are done playing. If you try to do it based on close, then it (probably) won't update if it is forcibly killed (such as through task manager or a crash).
The main reason I can think of for doing something on close is for any auto-saving. I don't know how RPG Maker would do this (probably requires a plugin) but you'd have it so anything that normally closes the game would be programmed instead to do "thing" and then close the game.
